messages:
tayla: Quick design check: compact eval rows are great for skimming but reviewers keep asking "why" after approve. How do we keep the reason visible without killing density? :mag:
hugo: Maybe a one-word reason pill plus a tiny chevron to expand details. Pill should read stronger than the model score so humans lead the glance.
sasha: For SR users the expand must be a real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls. Truncation is fine visually but not for assistive tech.
tayla: Microcopy options for pill: `brevity`, `style`, `accuracy`, or `Reason: brevity`. Which is clearest?
hugo: I vote just the word but bolder weight. "Reason:" feels noisy in a dense row.
sasha: Accessibility: when approving multiple items the toast should announce a preview like: `Approval saved for 3 items. Note preview: "{summary}"` and return focus to nearest diff. Use role=status polite.
dev-bot: Prototype tip: map Enter to open inline note, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter to submit. Show a 10s snackbar with Undo.
tayla: Copy for primary CTA candidates: A) `Confirm approval` B) `Approve and save note` C) `Approve (no note)`. We'll A/B test.
a11y-bot: Announcements nits: use polite live region, truncate preview by words, include `Reviewer note:` label, and ensure focus lands on the first visible diff after close. Also provide an accessible "Show full note" control for truncated content.
hugo: Action items: 1) design: pill + chevron mock (2 weights) 2) eng: keyboard mapping + snackbar undo 3) a11y: exact aria text and toast phrasing 4) PM to run a 5-person keyboard-first quick test.
tayla: I'll drop mocks and copy variants by EOD and tag you. :sparkles:
